steps.text: Marinate chicken in yogurt, garlic, ginger, and garam masala.
steps.safety_alert: Wash hands and clean surfaces after handling raw chicken.

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until browned, about 3 minutes per side.
steps.safety_alert: Watch out for splattering hot butter!

steps.text: Stir in tomato puree and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Pour in heavy cream and stir. Simmer for another 2 minutes before serving.
Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Add penne pasta and cook for 10 minutes until al dente.
steps.safety_alert: Be careful when handling boiling water!

steps.text: While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a pan. Sauté minced garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
steps.safety_alert: Do not let garlic burn or it will taste bitter.

steps.text: Add crushed tomatoes and simmer on low heat for 8 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh basil. Add the drained pasta, toss, top with Parmesan, and serve.
In a bowl, whisk flour, sugar, and baking powder. In another bowl, mix milk, egg, and melted butter.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently until just combined. The batter should be slightly lumpy.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Ladle batter onto the skillet. Cook until bubbles form on top, about 3 minutes.
Flip the pancakes and cook the other side until golden brown, about 2 minutes. Serve hot with maple syrup.
steps.safety_alert: Avoid touching the hot griddle surface.

steps.text: Rinse quinoa. Combine quinoa and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove quinoa from heat and let cool. Meanwhile, dice the cucumber and halve the cherry tomatoes.
steps.safety_alert: Use caution when chopping vegetables with a sharp knife.

steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Add the cooled quinoa, cucumbers, and tomatoes to the bowl. Toss to coat and serve chilled.
Mix yogurt and tikka spices. Coat paneer cubes and chopped bell peppers. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Sauté onions in a pan until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add marinated paneer and bell peppers. Cook for 8 minutes on medium heat, stirring occasionally.
steps.safety_alert: Be gentle so the paneer cubes do not break apart.

steps.text: Stir in cream, simmer for 2 minutes, and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). In a large bowl, whisk melted butter, brown sugar, and white sugar.
steps.safety_alert: Ovens get very hot, use oven mitts!

steps.text: Whisk in the egg until smooth. Slowly stir in the flour until a soft dough forms. Fold in chocolate chips.
Scoop dough balls onto a baking sheet. Bake for 10-12 minutes until edges are golden.
Remove from oven and let sit on the hot pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool.
steps.safety_alert: Cookies will be soft right out of the oven, handle with care.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and fry the chopped onion until deep golden, about 6 minutes.
steps.safety_alert: Hot oil can splatter; add the onion gently.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic and ginger paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pureed tomatoes, garam masala, and cumin. Simmer for 8 minutes until the sauce thickens and darkens.
Tip in the drained chickpeas with a splash of water. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lightly mash a few chickpeas to thicken, season with salt, and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti for 9 minutes until al dente. Reserve half a cup of pasta water before draining.
steps.safety_alert: Be careful lifting the pot of boiling water.

steps.text: While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat and add the sliced garlic.
Gently fry the garlic until pale gold, about 3 minutes, then stir in the red pepper flakes.
steps.safety_alert: Do not let the garlic brown or it will turn bitter.

steps.text: Add the drained spaghetti and a splash of the reserved pasta water. Toss for 1 minute so the sauce coats every strand.
Remove from heat, fold through the parsley, season with salt, and serve immediately.
Preheat the oven to 220C (425F) and place a baking tray inside to heat.
steps.safety_alert: The tray will be very hot; use oven mitts throughout.

steps.text: Spread the passata over each flatbread, leaving a thin border, and season lightly with salt.
Scatter the torn mozzarella evenly over the top and drizzle with olive oil.
Slide the flatbreads onto the hot tray and bake for 9 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are crisp.
Top with fresh basil leaves, slice, and serve hot.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over high heat until shimmering.
steps.safety_alert: A very hot wok can flare; keep a lid nearby.

steps.text: Add the garlic and diced vegetables and stir-fry for 4 minutes until just tender.
Add the cold cooked rice, breaking up any clumps, and toss for 3 minutes so it heats through and crisps slightly.
Pour in the soy sauce and sesame oil and stir-fry for another 1 minute.
Fold through the spring onions and serve immediately.
Butter one side of each slice of bread right to the edges.
Place one slice butter-side down in a cold non-stick pan and layer on the cheese, then top with the second slice, butter-side up.
Set the pan over medium-low heat and cook for 3 minutes until the underside is golden.
steps.safety_alert: The pan and melted cheese get very hot; use a spatula, not fingers.

steps.text: Flip carefully and cook the other side for 3 minutes until golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Rest for 1 minute, then cut in half and serve.
Add the cucumber chunks, tomato wedges, and sliced red onion to a large bowl.
steps.safety_alert: Take care slicing the onion with a sharp knife.

steps.text: Scatter over the olives and cubed feta.
Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano with a pinch of salt to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine without breaking up the feta.
Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the flavours meld, then serve.
Rub the chicken breasts with olive oil, paprika, salt, and pepper.
steps.safety_alert: Wash your hands and the board thoroughly after handling raw chicken.

steps.text: Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 minutes per side until the juices run clear.
steps.safety_alert: Ensure the chicken reaches 74C (165F) internally before serving.

steps.text: Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Divide the brown rice and spinach between two bowls and arrange the tomatoes and avocado on top.
Add the sliced chicken, squeeze over the lemon juice, and drizzle with a little olive oil to serve.
Preheat the oven to 180C (350F) and line an 8-inch square tin with baking paper.
steps.safety_alert: Use oven mitts whenever the oven is on.

steps.text: Gently melt the dark chocolate and butter together, stirring until smooth, then let cool slightly.
steps.safety_alert: Melt over low heat or in short microwave bursts so the chocolate does not scorch.

steps.text: Whisk in the sugar, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Fold in the flour and cocoa powder until just combined, then pour into the tin.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is set but the centre is still fudgy. Cool completely before slicing into squares.
Soak the glutinous rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Steam the soaked rice over simmering water for 20 minutes until tender and translucent.
steps.safety_alert: Steam is hot; lift the lid away from your face.

steps.text: Warm the coconut milk with the sugar and salt until dissolved, without boiling.
Pour most of the warm coconut mixture over the cooked rice, stir, and let it rest for 10 minutes to absorb.
Serve the sticky rice with sliced mango and drizzle the reserved coconut sauce on top.
